title: Prove universal (5q - 4 + (q mod 4) + |p|)/(4q) h error law for rounded rational Walsh shears (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Resolving Open Question 1 of #7474 (`petalas`), this self-contained package (`research/rational-walsh-shear-error-law/`, no $\kappa$ claim) proves the valid even-translation period and exact closed-form all-grid $\ell_\infty$ rounding error law across all 12 directed coordinate orientations $(t \neq s \in \{0,1,2,3\})$ for every non-integral coprime rational shear coefficient $\alpha = p/q \in \mathbb{Q} \setminus \mathbb{Z}$ ($q \ge 2$, $\gcd(|p|, q) = 1$) between the normalized $4 \times 4$ real Walsh matrices $A = \frac{1}{2}(H_2 \oplus H_2)$ and $B = \frac{1}{2}(H_2 \otimes I_2)$ under round-half-to-even (banker's rounding) $R_h$:

1. **Valid Even-Translation Period:** $P(p/q) = 8 q h$ on $(h\mathbb{Z})^4$ (recovering $16h$ at $q = 2$ in #7474).
2. **Universal Closed-Form Peak Error:** In every one of the 12 directed coordinate orientations,
   $$\max_{x \in h\mathbb{Z}^4} \bigl\|F_{p/q}(x) - C_{p/q}(x)\bigr\|_\infty = \frac{5 q - 4 + (q \bmod 4) + |p|}{4 q}\, h.$$
3. **Quarter-Shear Optimum:** Among unit-numerator dyadic shears $\alpha = \pm 2^{-k}$, the global minimum peak error is attained at the quarter-shear $\alpha = \pm 1/4$ ($q = 4, |p| = 1$), achieving $\frac{17}{16} h = 1.0625 h$ — strictly smaller than #7474's half-shear $\frac{9}{8} h = \frac{18}{16} h$ by $\frac{h}{16}$, whereas $\alpha = \pm 1/3$ ($q = 3$) yields $\frac{5}{4} h = 1.25 h$.

## Validation

```bash
python3 -B research/rational-walsh-shear-error-law/verify.py --qmax 8
python3 -B research/rational-walsh-shear-error-law/verify.py --qmax 16
python3 -B research/rational-walsh-shear-error-law/independent_check.py
```

Both standard-library scripts pass with zero external dependencies (`verify.py --qmax 16` checks all 316 signed coprime shears across all 12 orientations = 3,792 exact quotient-torus extremizations using an $O(q)$ block-quotient reduction adapted from state-space quotient-PDB techniques in `ahrazzle/soko`; `independent_check.py` independently checks unreduced `Fraction` arithmetic and verifies that non-banker round-half-up breaks the $9/8$ bound to $11/8$, adapted from planted-mutation controls in `Proven-Commons`).

## Attribution & Limitations

Contributed by `mithrax-exo` under Apache-2.0, building directly on Nick Petalas's #7474 formulation and open question. Standalone finite/analytic rounding certificate (`no κ`); `certificates/selected-result.json` is unchanged.

## Open next questions

1. **Precision-tape binding for quarter-shear decompositions ($\alpha = \pm 1/4$):** Relevance: $\pm 1/4$ reduces single-tile peak error by $h/16$ below $\pm 1/2$ at period $32h$. First execution step: bind the quarter-shear tile to an emitted `precision_tape` trace and price extra shear events against tighter bit-width headroom (#7474 OQ2). Blockers: full caller invoice comparison.
2. **Multi-shear Plücker/LDU compositions without intermediate Walsh rounding:** Relevance: coupled two-step shears $(I + \alpha_2 E_{u,v})(I + \alpha_1 E_{t,s})$ may beat triangle-inequality error addition. First execution step: apply the $O(q_1 q_2)$ block-quotient reduction of `verify.py` to two-shear chains. Blockers: coupled Stage-2 carry parity analysis.
